prompt: Which of these can a package have at full coverage? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Tests that check nothing
choices.why: Yes: a call with no assertion covers every line it reaches.

choices.text: A data race
choices.why: Yes: `count.go` reaches every statement in one run.

choices.text: A missing `if` for a case nobody wrote
choices.why: Yes: there is no line to be red.

choices.text: A statement no test ever ran
choices.why: That is exactly what lowers coverage below full.

prompt: A team requires 95% coverage on every pull request. What does the lesson predict?
hint: What does a target do to how tests are written?

choices.text: Defects like `Top`'s `-1` stop reaching production
choices.why: `Top` was at 100% with the defect inside.

choices.text: Races become visible in the coverage report
choices.why: Coverage cannot see a race; `-race` can.

choices.text: Tests written to move the number
choices.why: Right. Coverage is a map read by a person who decides, not a goal.

choices.text: Benchmarks become unnecessary
choices.why: Coverage says nothing about speed.
